lead.event: IDX’s temporary 7% auto-reject-bottom rule and subsequent adjustment
lead.headline: IDX cuts auto-reject lower price limit to 7% through 31 December
lead.blurb: The 7% auto-reject lower price limit took effect on 19 October, down from 15%, with an adjustment reported effective 20 October under the new rule. The policy runs through 31 December and will be reviewed in light of market conditions. IDX cited uncertainty over MSCI’s consultation on reclassifying Indonesia’s capital market from Emerging to Standalone.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: ADRO and AADI’s staged share buybacks
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: ADRO and AADI begin staged buybacks of up to Rp10 trillion
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Alamtri and Adaro Andalan each set a Rp5 trillion cap for their programs. Alamtri’s program runs for 12 months from 18 April, while Adaro Andalan’s runs until 22 May 2027.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Indonesian issuers’ buyback plans amid market volatility
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: BREN and other issuers plan Rp8.02 trillion in buybacks amid volatility
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Barito Renewables and BRPT each set aside up to Rp1 trillion, while CUAN and TPIA planned Rp500 billion and Rp1 trillion, respectively. BREN, BRPT and CUAN’s buyback periods run through 31 December, with TPIA’s ending 19 January.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Mandiri and BNI’s Additional Tier 1 capital issuances
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: BMRI and BBNI raise US$1.45 billion through AT1 issuances
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Mandiri issued a US$750 million perpetual bond in late September, while BNI completed a US$700 million AT1 issuance in April at a 7.15% annual yield. Both counted as additional core capital, and BNI plans to repurchase most of its 2021 AT1 instruments.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Telkom’s accelerated Rp4 trillion share buyback
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: TLKM prepares to accelerate share buyback of up to Rp4 trillion
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Telkom had more than Rp3 trillion of its approved allocation remaining as of 19 October. Funded from internal cash, the program was approved on 8 June and runs through 8 June 2027.

market_structure_policy.event: IDX and OJK capital-market reforms following MSCI scrutiny
market_structure_policy.headline: IDX plans to exclude 80 HSC stocks from IHSG after MSCI scrutiny
market_structure_policy.blurb: The stocks will remain listed and tradable, but their price movements will no longer affect the index. IDX will redistribute their weight to more liquid stocks with adequate free float and adjust the divisor to avoid an automatic index move. It will also label shareholders with 1% or more as affiliates or non-affiliates.

market_structure_policy.event: OJK’s Rp2.1 trillion sanctions on DSSA, BREN, and CUAN-related parties
market_structure_policy.headline: OJK imposes Rp2.1 trillion in sanctions tied to DSSA, BREN and CUAN
market_structure_policy.blurb: Dian Swastatika accounts for Rp1.5 trillion, Barito Renewables Rp500 billion and Petrindo Rp100 billion, following findings of share-trading manipulation and planned offering allocations to parties related to controlling shareholders. Petrindo said its fine was not imposed directly on the company, while Dian Swastatika said the sanction had no material impact on its finances or operations.

deals_control.event: WIFI’s 26.667% stake transfer to Sinergi Graha Kapital
deals_control.headline: WIFI shareholder transfers 26.667% stake to Sinergi Graha Kapital
deals_control.blurb: Solusi Sinergi Digital’s controlling shareholder, Investasi Sukses Bersama, transferred 1.42 billion shares at Rp2,870 each on 19 October, giving Sinergi Graha Kapital a 26.667% holding. Investasi Sukses Bersama’s stake fell to 27.756%, but it remained the company’s largest shareholder and controller, and the transfer did not change control.

deals_control.event: NSSS stake increase by Paradiso Resources
deals_control.headline: Paradiso Resources lifts NSSS stake to 5.85%
deals_control.blurb: Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera said Paradiso bought 414.63 million shares at Rp820 each on 15 October for Rp339.99 billion, for direct investment. Paradiso previously held 4.11%.

deals_control.event: Danantara’s merger of four investment managers into Mandiri Manajemen Investasi
deals_control.headline: Danantara completes four-manager merger into MMI with over Rp143 trillion in AUM
deals_control.blurb: Mandiri Manajemen Investasi became the receiving entity on 28 September, when Danantara Asset Management completed the merger. BNI Asset Management, BRI Manajemen Investasi and PNM Investment Management transferred all assets, liabilities, rights and obligations to it. The consolidation aims to build a larger-scale national investment manager.

earnings_guidance.headline: SSIA posts Rp262.6 billion first-half 2026 net profit
earnings_guidance.blurb: Surya Semesta's revenue rose 58.4% from a year earlier, turning a loss into profit. Management targets full-year revenue of Rp7.2 trillion and net profit of around Rp400 billion, but marketing sales reached just 24.1 hectares against a 135-hectare annual target.

earnings_guidance.event: Bank Mandiri’s business growth through August 2026
earnings_guidance.headline: BMRI reports bank-only assets up 20.7% through August
earnings_guidance.blurb: Bank Mandiri’s loans and third-party funds each grew 17.6% year on year, to Rp1,592 trillion and Rp1,687 trillion, respectively. Net profit rose 22.3% to Rp37.5 trillion, while third-party funds growth exceeded the banking industry’s 13.7%.

earnings_guidance.event: BSI’s remittance transaction volume through September 2026
earnings_guidance.headline: BRIS records Rp139 trillion in remittance transactions through September
earnings_guidance.blurb: BSI said integration with its e-channels helped lift remittance-service users by 15%. Corporate secretary Wisnu Sunandar said the bank expects this year’s remittance business growth to exceed last year’s, supported by 15 remittance partners across countries and 29 global partners.

earnings_guidance.event: TINS’s first-half results and 2026 production targets
earnings_guidance.headline: TINS posts Rp2.71 trillion first-half profit and targets 30,000 tons of 2026 output
earnings_guidance.blurb: Timah’s profit exceeded the Rp1.61 trillion full-year target set by market participants, while revenue reached Rp10.42 trillion, up 147% year on year. The company also targets sales of 25,000 metric tons, up 50% year on year.

macro_flows.event: MSCI’s consultation on Indonesia’s market classification and related responses
macro_flows.headline: MSCI consults on Indonesia reclassification as Goldman estimates US$5.6 billion outflows
macro_flows.blurb: Goldman Sachs’s estimate assumes Indonesian stocks are fully removed from MSCI indexes. MSCI cited investment-accessibility and market-governance concerns, will freeze several index changes during consultation and expects a final decision by 30 June 2027.

macro_flows.event: Bank Indonesia’s rupiah defense amid MSCI-driven market pressure
macro_flows.headline: Bank Indonesia defends rupiah amid MSCI pressure as it rises 0.28% to Rp17,992
macro_flows.blurb: Governor Destry Damayanti said President Prabowo ordered the central bank to act after the rupiah passed Rp18,000 per US dollar. BI intervened in spot, swap, NDF and DNDF markets and bought government securities in the secondary market. The rebound ended four consecutive days of weakening, with BI’s rate decision due 21 October.

macro_flows.event: Suahasil Nazara’s appointment as Indonesia’s Finance Minister
macro_flows.headline: Suahasil Nazara takes over as finance minister in third change in two years
macro_flows.blurb: A deputy minister since 2019, Suahasil replaced Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa on 14 September 2026. Purbaya had held the post since 8 September 2025. Economists from DPR Commission XI, CORE Indonesia, INDEF and Universitas Airlangga see the change as political consolidation and an effort to restore fiscal credibility, but not yet proof of a policy shift.
